answer: Sybil attackers mass-produce identities, so each must cost something real. In this bonded market, every agent posts collateral before earning, released only after probation. A cluster must fund that capital many times over, so forgery is a big, forfeitable outlay. To audit without trusting self-reports, the protocol emits a public beacon of verifiable randomness each epoch: bonded agents are sampled and any failure slashes the stake, so expected loss grows with the number of fakes. A hash anchor seals each record, blocking history erasure. A willow of co-signed vouches keeps newcomers solvent.
